title: Compact sections of a quasi-compact etale geometric fibre
statement:
Let $h:V\to T$ be a separated quasi-compact etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Set $V_{\bar t}=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with projection $r:V_{\bar t}\to V$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $I$ be the set of morphisms $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ satisfying $h\bar v=\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. Then $I$ is finite and the canonical morphism $\coprod_{\bar v\in I}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism over $\Omega$.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $F$ a constant-$A$ module sheaf on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $G=r^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Write $H^0_c(V_{\bar t},G)$ for the $A$-module of global sections of $G$ whose closed support of nonzero geometric germs, with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Every global section of $G$ has such support, and restriction to the components followed by the inverse-image germ identification gives a natural $A$-linear isomorphism
$$H^0_c(V_{\bar t},r^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{\bar v\in I}F_{\bar v},$$
where stalks are geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. More precisely, let $W\to T$ be etale, $\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ lie over $\bar t$, let $t:W\to V$ be a lift over $T$, and let $z\in F(W\xrightarrow{t}V)$. Extend $z$ by zero off the clopen graph of $t$ in $V\times_TW$. The pullback of this section to $V_{\bar t}$ maps to the germ of $z$ at $\bar w$ in the summand indexed by $t\bar w$, and to zero in every other summand.

proof.text: Put C = pullback h t and q = pullback.snd h t. Base-change instances give Etale q, IsSeparated q and QuasiCompact q. An etale morphism is locally quasi-finite, so Mathlib IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite, over the Artinian scheme Spec Omega, proves IsFinite q. This replaces the general normal-base decomposition.

proof.text: The pullback equivalence identifies I with the geometric fibre of the finite q at the identity; the existing GeometricFiber.finite instance proves I finite. Each canonical lift c(v) is an open immersion, since c(v) followed by the formally unramified q is the identity. Their opens are pairwise disjoint: an intersection lifts c(v′) through c(v), and composition with q forces that lift to be the identity. Every point is covered by GeometricFiber.exists_apply_default_eq. Thus nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of and the coproduct universal property prove the canonical Sigma.desc is an isomorphism. Empty fibres are included.

proof.text: Apply Etale.etaleModuleSection_closedSupport to each section of the pulled-back module sheaf. Its closed support, with the vanishing-ideal reduced induced subscheme, is proper: the subscheme immersion is closed and q is finite, hence proper, so their composite is proper by the existing instances. Therefore every section has proper support and the compactlySupportedSections inclusion is bijective.

proof.text: A scheme finite over Omega is finite discrete (finite_and_discreteTopology_of_isFinite); its residue fields are algebraically closed by Scheme.isAlgClosed_residueField_of_isClosed. The canonical component points give a bijection from I to the points of C. Apply the module-valued Etale.isIso_piLift_toPresheafFiber from ZeroDimensionalCohomology, then the canonical upperStarCompSheafFiberIso and reindex the finite product. The explicit finite direct-sum-to-product map is an isomorphism by DirectSum.addEquivProd. Its coordinate maps equal the component germs by canonical_coordinates. Cancellation proves exactly the stated compact-support restriction map is invertible.

proof.text: For the extension clause, the graph gamma is an open immersion because its composite with the etale second projection is identity, and a closed immersion because that projection is separated. Glue z and zero on its open complement using Scheme.Etale.existsUnique_of_pairwise_disjoint, specialized to module coefficients. Naturality of toPresheafFiber proves both restriction to z and zero germs off the graph.

source.place: Tags 09Z9, 03Q1 and 0F4Y; existing finite-fibre and module-valued site API, with elementary coordinate assembly

proof.text: The private unit_germ lemma proves compatibility for module coefficients by expanding upperStarCompSheafFiberIso, the general-site comap germ identities and Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. pullback_germ applies it to the actual etaleSectionPullbackToGlobal map. On a component v, the pointed image is b(v)=(v,w). If its underlying point lies on the graph, the open-immersion lifting property and the two pullback projections force v=w followed by lift. Thus all other component germs vanish; on this component toPresheafFiber_w_apply and restriction along gamma give the germ of z. The finite-sum lemma canonical_single proves the precise Sigma.ι equality.
